title: db.pool.exhausted during traffic spikes — connection held across payment retries
symptoms: During traffic spikes checkout requests fail with `db.pool.exhausted in_use=10 size=10` and `checkout.payment_failed order_id=... err=ConnectionPoolExhausted`. The database's own connection count sits well below its ceiling and scaling the DB does not help. Root cause is CheckoutHandler.process holding a ConnectionPool.acquire() connection across the whole PaymentClient.charge() retry loop, so slow-gateway retries drain DB_POOL_SIZE=10 under load.

steps.action: Confirm the exhaustion signal and that in_use has reached size
steps.outcome: Repeated db.pool.exhausted in_use=10 size=10 during the spike window confirms pool drain, not a DB outage

steps.action: Rule out real database capacity limits before treating it as a DB problem
steps.outcome: Database-side connection count is far below its ceiling — the application pool is the constraint

steps.action: Trace the connection's lifetime in code: CheckoutHandler.process acquires ConnectionPool.acquire() and holds it across PaymentClient.charge()
steps.outcome: Confirms the connection is held through PAYMENT_MAX_RETRIES=8 exponential-backoff attempts when the gateway is slow

steps.action: Move the acquire/release in checkout.py to wrap only the DB work, not the payment call (acquire after charge, or use a separate short-lived connection)
steps.outcome: The scarce pool connection is no longer tied up across gateway retries; the pool stops draining under load

steps.action: Optionally lower PAYMENT_MAX_RETRIES to cap worst-case hold time as a stopgap
steps.outcome: Bounds how long a slow charge can hold a connection while the code fix ships

title: Slow checkout, dashboards green — latency aggregation switched to avg
symptoms: Customers report checkout 'taking forever' but the checkout latency dashboard stays green and no alert fires. `metrics.latency name=checkout.duration agg=avg` looks nominal and CheckoutAPI.get_health passes throughout. The tail is hidden because a recent merge changed metrics.py LATENCY_AGGREGATION from p99 to avg, so p99-based SLO alerts went blind.

steps.action: Check the aggregation on the metrics.latency line for the affected window
steps.outcome: Confirms agg=avg rather than agg=p99 — the mean is masking tail latency

steps.action: Correlate against recent merges to metrics.py for a change to LATENCY_AGGREGATION
steps.outcome: Identifies the merge that switched LATENCY_AGGREGATION from 'p99' to 'avg' as the cause of the blind dashboard

steps.action: Revert LATENCY_AGGREGATION to p99 in metrics.py
steps.outcome: checkout.duration reports the tail again; the latency dashboard and alert regain visibility

steps.action: Add a test asserting SLO metrics aggregate on p99 so the aggregation cannot silently regress again
steps.outcome: Future merges that flip an SLO metric to avg fail CI before reaching production

title: payment.retry storm — gateway timeouts exhausting all attempts
symptoms: An elevated `checkout.payment_failed` rate pages on-call. Logs show `payment.retry order_id=... attempt=n/8 backoff=...s` climbing through all attempts, then `payment.exhausted order_id=... attempts=8` and `checkout.payment_failed order_id=... err=GatewayTimeout`. PaymentClient._call_gateway is exceeding PAYMENT_GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS on a large fraction of calls.

steps.action: Confirm the retry storm and where it terminates
steps.outcome: payment.retry climbing to attempt=8/8 then payment.exhausted attempts=8 confirms PaymentClient.charge is exhausting PAYMENT_MAX_RETRIES

steps.action: Determine whether GatewayTimeout is provider-wide or isolated to one AZ
steps.outcome: Global impact points at a provider outage; single-AZ concentration points at a network/ACL regression instead

steps.action: If provider-wide, communicate the outage to support and monitor payment.retry / payment.exhausted until the provider recovers
steps.outcome: Reduces duplicate tickets and confirms recovery when payment.retry volume returns to baseline

steps.action: Verify backoff spacing is correct so retries are not amplifying load on the degraded gateway
steps.outcome: Confirms PAYMENT_BASE_DELAY_SECONDS=0.5 (not a too-low value that would hammer the gateway between attempts)

title: fulfillment.queue.full — orders backing up, queue not draining
symptoms: `fulfillment.enqueued order_id=... depth=...` climbs steadily until `fulfillment.queue.full depth=5000 max=5000`, followed by `checkout.enqueue_failed order_id=... err=QueueFull`. Checkout and payment succeed but FulfillmentQueue.enqueue fails because the downstream fulfillment-worker consumer is not draining fast enough (under-scaled) or not at all (crashed).

steps.action: Check the fulfillment-worker consumer's pod status
steps.outcome: 0 Ready pods means a crashed consumer (zero drain); healthy-but-behind means under-scaling

steps.action: If the consumer is down, restart the fulfillment-worker deployment
steps.outcome: Consumer comes back healthy and the queue begins draining immediately

steps.action: If the consumer is merely behind, scale it up to exceed FulfillmentQueue.enqueue's arrival rate
steps.outcome: Consumption rate exceeds arrival rate; queue depth drains back toward baseline

steps.action: Watch FulfillmentQueue.depth() until it returns to near-zero baseline
steps.outcome: Confirms full recovery with no checkout.enqueue_failed errors; queued orders were held, not dropped
